name: Armv8-A 64-bit architecture
description: Arm added a 64-bit execution state, AArch64, to its application processor architecture alongside the 32-bit AArch32 state. AArch64 introduced the A64 instruction set, with fixed 32-bit instruction encodings and 64-bit general-purpose registers.

date.basis: Arm dates the first public preview to October 2011.

events.statement: Arm publicly previewed the Armv8-A architecture.

date.basis: The cover and revision history date issue 15.0 to 11 November 2011.

events.statement: Arm issued its first non-confidential instruction-set overview, including A64 for AArch64 execution.

evidence.supports: Dates the public issue and documents the 64-bit execution state and A64 encoding.

earliest_record.rationale: Arm's account dates the public architecture preview to October 2011. The November beta describes the instruction set at a separate dated stage.

research.note: The linked dependency concerns the AArch64 execution state and A64 instruction set within the original Armv8-A profile.
